pr_title: ConfigFlow default discovery without unique ID
pr_body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

This PR adds a default implementation for discovery to our configuration flow.
It allows for discovering integrations without the implementation of discovery logic and allows for discovering integration that cannot provide a unique ID to the configuration flow.

### Context

In [ADR-0011 - Discovery Requires Unique ID](https://github.com/home-assistant/architecture/blob/master/adr/0011-discovery-requires-unique-id.md), we have set a discovery to require a unique ID to allow the user to ignore any discovered item. This greatly enhanced the experience for the end-user and is awesome. However, this also means we can no longer offer discovered items that do not have a unique ID.

In issues #27292 (Gather zeroconf services) and #27371 (Gather Homekit models) an effort made by @balloob to gather discovery information for integrations. This is great! A lot of responses and information is given by users which can be used to enhance the user experience.

A couple of issues are created as a result of the above, which asks for the discovery to be implemented in the related integrations, for example: #32742, #32744.

### Problem

Implementing discovery using HomeKit, Zeroconf or SSDP discovery, requires coding. The flow needs to be extended to support the handling of the discovery.

This means we are dependent on contributors to handle the information from the "Gather" issues. It requires testing, and the contributor needs to have those devices in order to be able to implement it.

This makes the number of contributors that can contribute small and therefore progress slow.

Furthermore, the implementation requires a unique ID to be set in the configuration flow. This is great but leads to problems when the device does not expose one. In those cases often lead to a struggle in the PR reviews and in some cases, these requirements lead to dropping discovery for such an integration as the requirements cannot be met.

It is a shame we cannot leverage the provided data by our users to discover more items.

### Suggested solution

Currently, our discovery is part of the final "data" of the configuration entry. For example, by providing the unique ID, hostnames, or any other data that is exposed.

This PR aims to allow for "suggesting" an integration, without the need of providing any data to the integration, without the need for any implementation or allow cases where the unique ID cannot be provided. By implementing default discovery logic that leads to the same flow as when a user would have manually selected it from the add integration dialog (`async_step_user`).

Additionally, provide a method for implementers of discovery steps, to flag this discovery cannot be done with a unique ID to trigger similar logic.

This does, however, come with a couple of conditions to allow for these suggested discovered integrations:

- A discovered integration does not have any config entries
- A discovered integration does not have any other flows in progress

This is achieved by:

- Add a default discovery unique ID to identify these types of discovered items (`DEFAULT_DISCOVERY_UNIQUE_ID`).
    - Allows for these types of flows to be only triggered once.
	- Allows for ignoring these discovered items by the end-user.
	- Allows for resetting the `unique_id` to `None` when finishing the flow.
	- Allows for aborting default discovered config flow, when a config flow with an actual unique ID is added.
- Adding a default implementation for all discovery methods in our `ConfigFlow`. This allows for specifying discovery in the integration manifest, without the need for implementation. This default implementation will trigger `async_step_user`.

### Example: Abode

On March 12, Jonathan Simmons shared with us his discovery details for his Abode devices https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/27292#issuecomment-598419047

```
Manufacturer: Abode
Model: Iota
Home Assistant Integration: Homekit
Homekit model: Bridge
```

The Abode integration does have a configuration flow implemented but has not implemented any of the discovery methods.

Adding this in the current situation requires a contributor to have those devices and implement the discovery methods to handle this, however, it does implement the `async_step_user` method.

With the suggested implementation in this PR, we can simply add the data to the manifest:

```json
{
  "domain": "abode",
  "name": "Abode",
  "config_flow": true,
  "documentation": "https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/abode",
  "requirements": ["abodepy==0.19.0"],
  "codeowners": ["@shred86"],
  "homekit": {
    "models": ["Abode", "Iota"]
  }
}
```

And after that, it will work:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/195327/84565672-e3e81d80-ad6a-11ea-9483-bf5f4bf7a4f5.png)

Clicking "Configure" will simply trigger the `async_step_user` method, and ignoring works as well.

### Example: Tellduslive

The tellduslive integration does provide additional discovery logic, but doesn't have a unique ID available to set.

As there is additional handling, the default provides methods won't work, thus a helper method (`_async_handle_discovery_without_unique_id`) can be used to achieve the same:

```python
    async def async_step_discovery(self, user_input=None):
        """Run when a Tellstick is discovered."""
        await self._async_handle_discovery_without_unique_id()

        _LOGGER.info("Discovered tellstick device: %s", user_input)
        if supports_local_api(user_input[1]):
            _LOGGER.info("%s support local API", user_input[1])
            self._hosts.append(user_input[0])

        return await self.async_step_user()
```

With this implementation, discovery will work (once), can be ignored, and the resulting entry does not have a unique ID (because there isn't one).

### Example: IPP

The IPP integration is great! As it can integrate with tons of printers out there from different manufacturers. This is also the source of the problems it has, those different manufacturers all deliver different info in the discovery information.

One delivers a unique identifier, others have zero useable information. This causes the following right now:

**If a printer cannot provide a unique ID, the only solution is to abort discovery. (Which the IPP integration does).**

This is not so nice, because if one has a printer that works with this integration, even with this missing identifier, the integration could still be offered to the user.

```python
        if unique_id:
            await self.async_set_unique_id(unique_id)
            self._abort_if_unique_id_configured(
                updates={
                    CONF_HOST: self.discovery_info[CONF_HOST],
                    CONF_NAME: self.discovery_info[CONF_NAME],
                },
            )

        await self._async_handle_discovery_without_unique_id()
        return await self.async_step_zeroconf_confirm()
```

Implemented in: <https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/36754/commits/49b8ff55380b7f92a38ae559a9d5c07c6987e2d2>

The same conditions still apply automatically: No IPP config entries exist, a flow that does have a unique ID takes preference.

issue_context.title: Add homekit discovery to abode
issue_context.body:
Home Assistant supports proposing a config flow to users based on Homekit discovery. This is done based by specifying [homekit in your manifest](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/creating_integration_manifest#homekit) and adding a config flow step `async_step_homekit`.

Once discovered, we can prompt users to log in to Abode via user/pass.

Abode has been found in our [gathered Homekit models](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/27292).
comments: Hey there @shred86, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`abode`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L16) for? Thanks!

There hasn't been any activity on this issue recently. Due to the high number of incoming GitHub notifications, we have to clean some of the old issues, as many of them have already been resolved with the latest updates.
Please make sure to update to the latest Home Assistant version and check if that solves the issue. Let us know if that works for you by adding a comment 👍
This issue now has been marked as stale and will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.
This is still a thing that we should do.

review_comments: We should make the frontend capture this key and translate it without requiring every integration to translate it
It is mainly here for completeness and pleasing the CI for this method to exists.

I'm confused by this logic. When can this happen? If this can happen when both SSDP and Zeroconf are configured, would we then require the config flow to call `async_handle_discovery_without_unique_id` ? 

I think that we should just expect developers that implement discovery to implement all types of discovery.

I think it makes the implementation easier, as it allows one to call this method without having to worry about it.
I've added the IPP example use-case to the PR description to show why.
